data.body:
Plan-review returned BLOCK on the re-review; all four findings were REAL and are now fixed.

I verified each against the tree before editing rather than taking the reviewer's word:

| # | Claim in plan | Reality (verified) |
|---|---|---|
| B1/B2 | retention sweeps "the oldest per-release tags beyond `DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN` (default 3)" | `grep -rn DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN .` -> **no matches anywhere**. `mcp_reconcile_orphans` keeps live + prev and sweeps CONTAINERLESS orphaned per-release tags. There is no keep-N-oldest semantic. |
| A1 | alarm `rebar-docker-unaccounted-overlay2` | `monitoring_autodeploy.tf:469` declares `alarm_name = "rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes"`; the runbook uses the same. The AC pins alarms BY NAME, so the plan named a non-existent artifact. |
| A2 | `systemctl enable --now docker` is "today's first side-effecting step, line 55" | it is at `compose-up.sh:88`, and `dnf install -y docker` at `:53` runs earlier — so it is neither line 55 nor the first side-effecting step. |

All three passages now match the code.

## The part that corrects me

Earlier in this ticket I recorded AC6 as satisfied and cited
`test_the_retention_sweep_spares_the_serving_release_and_the_rollback`. That citation was right,
and it is exactly what shows the plan was wrong: "the serving release and the rollback" IS
live+prev. The tests encode live+prev; the plan prose claimed a retain-3 count. I checked the ACs
against the tests and did not check the DESIGN section against the code, so I passed over a
mechanism that was never built. The reviewer caught what I missed.

## Why this belongs to tonight's pattern

`DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN` is a knob that exists only in prose. Anyone reading this plan to extend the
retention policy would have gone looking for a configuration point that was never implemented, and
found the live+prev sweep instead. It is the documentation form of the same failure running through
this whole epic — an artifact asserting a capability that is not in effect — which is why the fix
is to restate the plan to match `mcp_reconcile_orphans`, not to invent the knob to match the plan.

Re-running `review-plan` now. The code is unchanged throughout: every correction here is to the
plan text, and the merged implementation (`bbe5d228bd2f`) was correct in all four places.
